chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ and ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said: We asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the maʾmūmah wound, so he said:
In it is one-third of the diyah, and in the jāʾifah is one-third of the diyah, and in the mūḍiḥah are five camels.

key_terms.اَلدِّيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury or wrongful harm
key_terms.اَلْإِبِلِ: camels, the unit used here for assessing diyah
key_terms.اَلْجَائِفَةِ: a wound that penetrates into the body cavity
key_terms.اَلْمُوضِحَةِ: a wound that exposes the bone
key_terms.خَمْسٌ: the fixed quantity of compensation specified here

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for a maʾmūmah, jāʾifah, and mūḍiḥah wound in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for compensation in specific bodily injuries. It states that the compensation for the maʾmūmah and the jāʾifah is one-third of the diyah, while the compensation for the mūḍiḥah is five camels.
